![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/9c5d2e2426a817b62f8cd834d7d31786c5f2dfd52a7b784fd0bf337abed6c4fc.png)

Consider the region bounded by $y={e}^{2-x}$ and $y={e}^{{x}^{2}},$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={e}^{2-x}$ and $g(x)={e}^{{x}^{2}}.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ {e}^{2-x} & ={e}^{{x}^{2}} \\ 2-x & ={x}^{2} \\ 0 & ={x}^{2}+x-2 \\ (x+2)(x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $x=-2$ to $x=1.$

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/8a7f49165698bdac791a31a058c3228e6e2beab9f5ee9393971aa0e9aecd27b8.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=g(x)={e}^{{x}^{2}},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=f(x)={e}^{2-x}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1}({[{e}^{2-x}]}^{2}-{[{e}^{{x}^{2}}]}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1}({e}^{4-2x}-{e}^{2{x}^{2}})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
